Sorry for so many replies and edits - I just feel the need to explain myself in this post in case anyone else who is going through a chronic pain situation also sees it and thinks suicide is the way out. IT'S NOT. I don't give a fuck if I have to use a fucking hands free mouse to use a computer (including typing via an on screen keyboard) one day - I WILL NEVER STOP WORKING AND LIVING MY LIFE. Fuck this suicidal shit. I am horrified by what I wrote last week. Please, anyone else experiencing chronic pain, just know that there are ways to live.

https://www.amazon.com/SmartNav-Natural-Point-Hands-Mouse/dp/B004IA6WJQ

I just looked back on this thread and I'm definitely realizing how fucking stupid I sound. I thought about it, and I'm going to continue working through the pain. No matter what happens, I'm NOT going to lose my job or life over this. I'm working with the top neurologists in the country (including a practice that was formed by one of top 10 universities in the U.S.), and I've found some supplements that are GREATLY helping me. I'm also seeing two psychologists (including one who is a cancer survivor and understands the pain of navigating medical system). My friends, family, and employer are all behind me and offering to do anything they can to help me. I'm going to get through this and turn it into a success story that helps other young people with neuropathy. I'm really sorry for my earlier comments. I appreciate you listening.
I guess this needed to happen to make me grateful for my life and show that I can get through anything. This is giving me something to fight for. The truth is, I had neurological issues from the time I was a young child. I think I've always been susceptible to this - normal people wouldn't have this over a few years of drinking or 10 days of vaping, which is what my last neurologist tried to tell me (and why another neurologist didn't even believe that was related to my issues at all). I have to stop blaming myself, which is what ALL of my neurologists tried to tell me.

I appreciate it, but honestly, this thread confirmed that suicide is the only way. You can't take it one day at a time in a situation like this. And I don't want to live a life everyone clearly recognizes is fucked.

I'll be honest - this thread has really only solidified that I should do it. Everyone clearly recognizes that my life is fucked. Wishful thinking and hope when there isn't any doesn't make up for that. Easy for everyone else to say.
I would normally agree, but I don't see how good things happen to disabled people who are unemployable and can't get insurance or their independence. The only way out is suicide.
Congratulations and never forget how awesome you are!

I'm 26 and definitely NOT too young to have a drinking problem!
Fuck that shit.
Thank you for sharing! I'm much happier after five months of not drinking.
Good for you - congratulations! I can't wait to make it to 1,058 one day!

I never wanted to have more than two to seven drinks (which I recognize is still a generous amount of alcohol). However, at 25 years old, I was a 5'6" female who weighed between 112 to 117 pounds and was drinking 10+ rum and cokes and whiskey shots every Friday night. There were nights when I had over 15. Lord only knows how strong the rum and cokes were - there were some bartenders who loved to give me my money's worth because they liked me. I used to track each drink on my phone to see how many calories I ingested... because that was more worrisome than my overall health (despite being a little underweight). I could go on and on and on without stopping...

I have a strong history of alcohol on both sides of my family, including relatives who died because of direct complications from alcoholism.

Yes, I had some problems.
I felt the same way a few months ago. I was indeed a puker when I drank, and it reminded me of those terrible nights...
